title: Ingress Congestion Probe — lab notebook
content:
Quick lab notebook for a lightweight congestion-probing approach at the HTTP/gRPC ingress layer. 

Purpose:
- Detect transient and sustained congestion inside the ingress tier (LB -> ingress-router -> runtime) without requiring heavyweight load tests.
- Provide a low-cost API that frontends (and SDKs) can use to probe path capacity and adapt client-side concurrency/batching.
- Surface signals to Console/Optimize for routing and autoscale policy tuning.

Background/context (why this):
- We see bursts where tail latency spikes even when backend util is moderate — hypothesis: transient queueing in ingress (connection queues, proxy goroutine pools, per-tenant token-buckets).
- Heavy-weight synthetic tests are noisy and expensive; need on-path lightweight probes.

High-level idea: small non-impactful probe requests that exercise typical code paths (auth, token validation, routing, initial KV cache lookup) and return a compact telemetry envelope. Probes are cheap (tiny token cost) and can be scheduled by SDK or run by the edge sidecar.

Probe API shape (draft):
- endpoint: POST /v1/_probe/congestion
- auth: same token as normal request (so probes exercise auth & tenant plumbing)
- payload (json):
{
  "probe_id": "<uuid>",
  "probe_type": "latency-sample|queue-depth|route-check",
  "payload_hint": "short|empty|warm-kv",
  "trace_sample": true|false,
  "client_ts": "2026-01-10T12:00:00Z"
}
- response: 200 plus small telemetry envelope in body and optional header X-RW-Probe (compact base64):
{
  "probe_id": "<uuid>",
  "server_ts": "2026-01-10T12:00:00Z",
  "latency_ms": 12.3,
  "ingress_queue_ms": 3.2,
  "route": "/v1/generate",
  "backend_variant": "gptx-8q",
  "ok": true
}

Notes about fields:
- ingress_queue_ms: best-effort measurement captured by instrumenting the earliest point after request dequeued (or a proxy hook). May be missing when not applicable.
- route: canonical target path the probe was routed through (we want to ensure probes exercise same paths as normal requests).
- backend_variant: which model/variant selected (helps detect variant-specific queuing).

Server-side implementation sketch:
- Lightweight handler that runs minimal validation + a small routing decision and returns telemetry. MUST NOT allocate large KV caches or long-lived resources.
- Instrumentation points: accept timestamp, dequeue timestamp, handler-enter timestamp, handler-exit timestamp. Use these to compute queueing and service times.
- Sampling: default 1 probe / 5s per client-key during sustained activity, 5x higher sample during SLO violations. SDK sidecar should back off if probes start getting 429.

Client/SDK behavior:
- Use probes to adapt concurrency/batch sizes. Example heuristic: if recent probes show ingress_queue_ms > 10ms and latency_ms > 100ms, reduce inflight by 20% and lower batch size.
- Send probes as ordinary authenticated requests so they exercise tenant limits. Probe responses include a `discount` field if token-cost-free (for experiments).

ASCII diagram (ingress flow, rough):

CLIENT/SDK --(request)--> EDGE PROXY (L7) --(dequeue)--> INGRESS ROUTER --(route decision)--> ROUTE POOL -> RUNTIME -> MODEL
  |                             |                        |
  |---- probe hooks ----------- | -----------------------|

Probe hits early codepaths (auth -> route decision) and returns before queuing heavy runtime work.

Experiment plan (short):
1) Canary on dev cluster: enable probe endpoint behind feature flag. Run SDK emulator to send probes mimicking real clients. Compare queue_ms to p99 latency.
2) Add ingress-side metric: probe_success_rate, probe_avg_queue_ms, probe_route_histogram. Hook to console.
3) Run controlled spike test: 200 small probes/sec + 100 real requests/sec. Observe correlation between probe_queue_ms and tail latency.

Preliminary heuristics we may expose in SDK (config example):
{
  "probe_config": {
    "enabled": true,
    "sample_rate_per_minute": 12,
    "burst_sample_multiplier": 4,
    "max_concurrent_probes": 2,
    "failure_backoff_ms": 1000
  }
}

Open questions / tradeoffs (brain dump):
- Does probe traffic change scheduling behavior? (e.g., cause preemption of small tasks vs large) — need to ensure probes are deprioritized if necessary.
- Cost accounting: should probes be billable? For production customers this is sensitive. We can mark probes as zero-cost during experiment but need an audit trail.
- Security: probes use same auth tokens; could they be abused to fingerprint infra? Add rate limits by token and source IP.
- Privacy/compliance: telemetry contains route/variant hints — ensure no PII sent; sanitize.
- Consistency across Dedicated/Private: Private deployments might disable probes by default. Guard with config.

Edge cases and failure modes: 
- Probes themselves can be throttled or queued; need a fallback so SDK can detect probe suppression (e.g., if probe fails with 429 for > N times, switch to passive telemetry).
- Distributed clocks: rely on client_ts/server_ts delta for skew; if skew > 500ms, mark as unreliable. Long-term: consider using server-side monotonic counters instead.

Quick checklist (for next steps):
- [ ] Add lightweight handler + unit tests in ingress repo (PR stub: linked above).
- [ ] Add metrics and tag with tenant, route, variant.
- [ ] Implement SDK probe scheduler + backoff logic.
- [ ] Run dev canary + synthetic spike. Capture dataset.
- [ ] Decide billing policy (experiment vs GA).

Experiment logs to attach later: small CSVs of (ts, probe_id, client_ts, server_ts, latency_ms, ingress_queue_ms, route). Will use to compute cross-correlation and Granger-ish test for predictive power.

Notes-to-self: keep probes minimal so they don't interact with shard-reservation or warm-kv prefetching; probe payload_hint should influence how router picks warm vs cold lane.

Reference heuristics:
- If probe_queue_ms shows 95th > 25ms across 1m window -> ingress backpressure alert.
- If probe_success_rate drops < 90% while real-requests success_rate remains > 95% -> probes being deprioritized; mark as unreliable.

Small example probe response (as string for testing):
{
  "probe_id": "5a8f3c2e-1234-4b12-9f0e-abcdef012345",
  "server_ts": "2026-01-10T12:03:45.123Z",
  "latency_ms": 24.6,
  "ingress_queue_ms": 6.5,
  "route": "/v1/chat/completions",
  "backend_variant": "gpt-3.8-q",
  "ok": true
}

Random todos for implementation:
- instrument earliest dequeue hook in envoy/proxy (Jonas to prototype)
- verify how tenant throttles affect probe response code (Maya)
- add opt-in flag in private deploy helm charts

If this looks promising we can fold into 'ingress telemetry v2' workstream and add a small UI panel in Console: probe health + suggested adaptive concurrency.

End of notebook for now — will paste experiment outputs here in next iteration.

-- Ravi
